venue_requirements.source_profile: MICCAI 2026 submission guidelines and Springer LNCS proceedings style
venue_requirements.main_text_scope: Title, abstract, keywords, main body, figures, tables, conclusion, and acknowledgments/disclaimer if present must fit within the main text page limit.
format_policy: Use the official MICCAI/LNCS template without margin, spacing, or author-block modifications.
Submit a searchable PDF; keep the manuscript self-contained for review.
Anonymize acknowledgments, links, repositories, and data-use statements when needed for double-blind review.
Declare data origin, license, and ethics/approval information when applicable, preferably in the experimental setup.

observed_moves: Start from a clinical WSI or computational pathology bottleneck, then state the technical gap.
Introduce one compact method idea with a pipeline figure or algorithmic module instead of a broad survey.
Use experiments to define datasets, splits, baselines, metrics, and ablations before interpreting results.
Report results through tables and figures, including external validation or ablation only when supported.
Keep clinical translation claims cautious; reviewers scrutinize validation, reproducibility, and unsupported SOTA language.
pathology_topics_to_cover_when_relevant: multiple instance learning for gigapixel WSIs
weak, self, or vision-language supervision under limited annotations
reproducibility through code, splits, deterministic metrics, and evidence locks

claim_discipline.numeric_claims: All numeric results must come through metric placeholders or locked result blocks; never type raw metric values.
claim_discipline.citation_claims: Use selected citation placeholders only; the abstract has no citations.
claim_discipline.clinical_claims: Avoid clinical deployment, real-world readiness, or broad generalization unless external evidence explicitly supports it.
claim_discipline.sota_claims: Use SOTA/outperforms/significant language only when baseline and statistical evidence exist in the evidence lock.
claim_discipline.section_separation: Experiments defines protocol; Results reports findings; Discussion interprets and limits claims.

locked_block_requirements.policy: Do not rewrite locked block facts in prose; frame or interpret them with cautious MICCAI prose.

abstract.purpose: Summarize the WSI study for a MICCAI/LNCS reader in one compact evidence-locked paragraph.
must_include: clinical or computational pathology problem
one-sentence method summary grounded in the locked method evidence
cohort and evaluation setting only at a high level
strongest supported result through metric placeholders when available
bounded conclusion about what the evidence supports
abstract.metrics_policy: Use metric placeholders for any numeric result; include only headline supported metrics.
abstract.figures_tables_policy: Do not include figures or tables.
must_avoid: raw cohort counts not present in locked evidence

introduction.purpose: Motivate the MICCAI contribution and lead to clear evidence-bounded claims.
must_include: medical imaging or WSI motivation tied to a concrete pathology need
why weak supervision, MIL, or evidence-locked reporting is needed
clear gap in current model reporting, validation, or reproducibility practice
short overview of the proposed PathLab-backed approach
explicit contribution list phrased cautiously and supported by planned evidence
introduction.citation_policy: Use selected references for WSI/MIL/background and preserve required citations from the literature draft.
introduction.metrics_policy: Avoid detailed results; only preview evaluation goals without numbers.
introduction.figures_tables_policy: May refer to an overview figure if it is ready in the manifest; do not force a figure here.
introduction.tone: Conference style: focused, problem-driven, and novelty-forward.
must_avoid: results interpretation better suited for Results or Discussion

related_work.purpose: Position the method and evidence-locking choices against verified prior work.
must_include: weakly supervised WSI or MIL methods
attention, prototype, graph, state-space, or vision-language model family most relevant to the run
clinical validation and external validation context
reproducibility context: code, data splits, deterministic evaluation, or evidence-locked reporting
what remains different about the PathLab evidence-locked workflow
related_work.citation_policy: Use only selected references; include all required related-work citations.
related_work.metrics_policy: Do not compare numeric results unless those numbers are in locked evidence.
related_work.tone: Thematic rather than paper-by-paper; comparative but fair.

methods.purpose: Describe the PathLab method and reproducible implementation without rewriting locked facts.
must_include: model and end-to-end pipeline overview
the literal method locked block input for deterministic configuration facts
training, inference, feature extraction, or MIL aggregation workflow if available
privacy scrubbing and provenance handling
guardrail that factual configuration comes from locked blocks
methods.citation_policy: Cite method-family references where needed, but keep locked implementation facts uncited unless literature support is needed.
methods.metrics_policy: Do not report outcome metrics here.
methods.figures_tables_policy: May include a ready method overview figure; do not invent architectural diagrams.
methods.tone: Technical and implementation-oriented but compact for MICCAI page limits.
must_avoid: duplicating locked block details in prose

experiments.purpose: Specify dataset, split, baseline, and evaluation protocol separately from results interpretation.
must_include: dataset, split, and external-validation status from locked evidence
evaluation metrics and model-selection protocol without raw values
baseline, ablation, and external-validation roles when available
statistical test, confidence interval, or calibration protocol only if present in evidence
experiments.citation_policy: Use references only for standard evaluation protocols or baseline families when selected.
experiments.metrics_policy: Name metrics but do not give values; values belong in Results through placeholders.
experiments.figures_tables_policy: Include dataset/split tables only if present in table_paths.
must_avoid: claims about superiority or clinical impact

results.purpose: Report the supported empirical findings with tables, figures, and metric placeholders.
must_include: main result from the locked results block
primary table when available
all ready figures from the manifest
external validation findings only when evidence exists
ablation findings only when evidence exists
uncertainty, CI, or statistical evidence when locked
results.citation_policy: Citations are optional and should not distract from locked empirical evidence.
results.metrics_policy: Every numeric result must use metric placeholders; never type raw numbers.
results.figures_tables_policy: Every ready manifest figure must be included with its path and figure_id; tables must come only from table_paths.

discussion.purpose: Interpret the results for a MICCAI audience while bounding all claims to evidence.
must_include: interpretation of what the main evidence suggests
why evidence locking and provenance matter for MICCAI pathology review
limitations from missing evidence, cohort scope, split design, or external validation
cautious clinical relevance without deployment claims
future work tied to concrete missing evidence
discussion.citation_policy: Use citations sparingly for clinical validation or reproducibility context.
discussion.metrics_policy: Refer to reported results qualitatively or via metric placeholders only when necessary.
discussion.figures_tables_policy: Usually no new figures or tables.
must_avoid: turning limitations into unsupported clinical promises

conclusion.purpose: Close the MICCAI paper with a short evidence-bounded contribution and scope.
must_include: short statement of the evidence-locked paper generation contribution
supported empirical takeaway
bounded future-facing implication for reproducible computational pathology
conclusion.metrics_policy: Avoid new metrics; if needed, reuse placeholders already reported.
